obligations: Explicit normalized Vandermonde forms exist for every n>=2 and r>n.
Every n forms, and hence every smaller subset, are linearly independent.
Unit coefficient normalization gives strictly negative genuine selecting weights on the unit ball.
Equal p>r/n implies p>1 and the target ideal is the linear hyperplane ideal by the existing smooth-center formula.
At every nonzero point at most n-1 forms vanish.
Vanishing forms give independent holomorphic normal coordinates; the nonvanishing factors stay bounded below locally.
Each complex normal integral of |w|^-2/p is finite for p>1.
Compact-annulus local integrability and homogeneity give finite positive angular integral A.
Radial Tonelli gives I=A/[2(n-r/p)] finite for p>r/n.
The construction checks both individual divisor poles and their common intersection.
Every global ideal section vanishes at the origin, so every admissible g has g(0)=1.
Circle mean value applies because lambda->g(lambda z) has a radius exceeding one for every z inside the ball.
Tonelli and unit-circle invariance give integral |g|^2>=Vol(B), also for infinite norms.
The constant g=1 is admissible and attains Vol(B)=pi^n/n!.
The reciprocal sum ranges over [1,n) when r/n<p<=r; this disproves the unqualified planar zero-regime extension.
The lower ratio is a concrete positive bound for equal-exponent universal constants, without determining optimality.
